approach.why: Static probes over the parsed final schema (Probe F: ITEM_SIDE tables pinned by name, NOT NULL + ON DELETE CASCADE on feedback_id, plus a generic no-SET-NULL rule for user-keyed FKs to feedback) and over route-literal homes (Probe E: each C43/C44 path pinned to its registering fn, that fn to the lib.rs export name build_app merges, and that name to Probe A's class) is the right shape: each probe fails on the defect it names and names the artefact it defends. Verified on the merged tree: both oracles exit 0 with Probe F clean and Probe E PASS; replays of F2 and H2 from the README rows on a scratch copy exit 1 as recorded. The diff is additive (208 insertions, 5 deletions all in README/oracle.json prose and version strings); no existing probe's code changed, so nothing was weakened. Every deliverable the objective names is present: erasure v1.1.0 Probe F, host-tenant-binding v1.1.0 Probe E, M12 recorded for public-board-moderation-gate at v1.2.0. The concerns below are parser boundaries of the probes, not design faults.

findings.summary: Probe F stays green when a later migration DROPs the CASCADE FK: parse_schema never models DROP CONSTRAINT, so an end-user-keyed row can be left behind with the oracle passing
findings.evidence: .claude/project-oracles/feedback-erasure-completeness/oracle.py:460-478 handles ADD COLUMN / ADD CONSTRAINT / DROP COLUMN / ALTER COLUMN NOT NULL only; no branch for DROP CONSTRAINT. Probe B's raw-count guard (oracle.py:446, `REFERENCES feedback`) is unchanged by such a statement. Reproduced on a scratch copy via --root: added migrations/00099_drop_fk.sql = `ALTER TABLE feedback_not_needed DROP CONSTRAINT feedback_not_needed_feedback_id_fkey;` -> `PASS feedback-erasure-completeness`, `Probe B (FK cascade completeness): clean`, `Probe F (item-side board artefacts): clean`, exit 0. The README row for F says 'a dropped or renamed table fails'; a dropped constraint does not. No behavioural backstop: grep for feedback_not_needed|board_priority_entries|feedback_board_notes under crates/feedbackmonk-api/tests/ matches only tests/board_session.rs (2 hits), none in tests/me_feedback_delete.rs. Pre-existing parser limitation inherited by F, not introduced here; fix is to model DROP CONSTRAINT (Postgres default <table>_<col>_fkey plus named constraints) and record it as F5.

findings.summary: Probe E sees only .route("<full path>") literals: a C43 route made reachable through .nest(prefix, Router::new().route("/session", ..)) inside another classified router (e.g. unbound health_router) passes A and E
findings.evidence: .claude/project-oracles/host-tenant-binding/oracle.py:664: the only registration shape searched is a regex for `.route(` followed by the quoted full path; Probe A's .nest ban applies to build_app's chain only (README Probe A row). Reproduced on a scratch copy via --root: crates/feedbackmonk-api/src/router.rs health_router given `.nest("/api/v1/projects/:project_id/board", Router::new().route("/session", get(health::liveness)))` -> `PASS host-tenant-binding`, Probe A PASS, Probe E PASS, exit 0, while the session exchange is now reachable on the unbound, un-rate-limited router. The README states the literal-only scope ('as a .route("<path>" literal'), so the claim is honest but narrower than 'registered only inside its home fn'. Fix: fail any .nest( in the api crate whose prefix is a prefix of a ROUTE_HOMES path, or any .nest( outside the two home fns; record as H5.

findings.summary: Probe F's generic guard iterates only FKs that target feedback, so a user-keyed table that names the item by short_code with no FK is invisible to the item side; Probe E (user side) still forces its erasure
findings.evidence: oracle.py:759 `if f.target != "feedback" ...: continue` -- tables with no FK to feedback never enter the loop. Scratch copy via --root: added migrations/00099_flags.sql creating board_item_flags(tenant_id, project_id, item_short_code TEXT, user_sub TEXT) -> Probe F clean, but `Probe E (end-user table coverage) failures: ... table board_item_flags carries end-user key column(s) ['user_sub'] but is not erased by a DELETE scoped (tenant, project, key = end_user_sub)`, exit 1. So 'forget me' (FR-FBR-60 person side) holds; item deletion leaving other viewers' rows on a gone item is outside every probe. Not a defect in the tree; a boundary to name in the README's 'Known static boundary' style.

findings.summary: The 15 mutations (E5-E8, F1-F4, M12, H1-H4) exist only as one-line README rows; the lead replayed them by hand, and re-verification after the next parser change means re-deriving each from prose
findings.evidence: .claude/project-oracles/feedback-erasure-completeness/README.md:63-80, host-tenant-binding/README.md:104-117, public-board-moderation-gate/README.md:94-100 record mutation text only; `git diff --stat 9b09a61..5e4431c` shows no script under .claude/project-oracles/**. Consistent with the project's precedent (28 host-tenant-binding mutations, M1-M11, all prose). Re-deriving F2 and H2 from the rows took a few lines each and matched (exit 1), so the record is usable; a checked-in mutations.py --root <scratch> applying each row to a copy and asserting exit 1 then 0 would make the table a program (mode: oracle self-check; owner: each oracle directory). Never a blocker.
